identity_evidence.quote: The patient was a 53-year-old female with progressive HL.

attribution_limitations: Implanted side (left or right ear) is not stated in the text; the Figure 1 caption names right and left ear audiogram line styles only.
The 2023 genetic testing and the next-generation sequencing result are not identified in the source as the same event.

Speech audiometry, hearing level with EAS, hearing preservation and the text impedance comparison are stated without a time point in the sentences that report them; the methods list 1, 3, 6 and 12 month evaluations generally, and the printed text 12 months post-op under Figure 4C is image text only. Only the Figure 6 caption finding carries a caption-stated post-operative time.

The surgical-technique sentences (less-invasive procedure, round window exposure, slow insertion) carry no date; they are grouped with the February 2024 electrode use because they describe insertion of that electrode, but the date is stated only in the electrode-use sentence.

claims.text: A 53-year-old woman with progressive hearing loss noticed at around age 20 visited otorhinolaryngology at age 52 because of insufficient hearing with hearing aids. Genetic testing was conducted in 2023, and comprehensive next-generation sequencing identified a mitochondrial m.1555A > G variant as the cause, with no other affected family members. Her audiogram showed precipitous high-frequency loss with residual hearing in the lower frequencies.

claims.text: After a pre-operative audiogram, she received electric-acoustic stimulation with a dexamethasone-eluting FLEX28 DEX electrode array in a clinical trial in February 2024. The round window membrane was exposed with a low-speed drill and the electrode slowly inserted, with intraoperative cochlear microphonics monitoring; the maximum response occurred when the first electrode reached the 500 Hz area, and after full insertion the largest response came from the third electrode.

evidence.quote: Audiograms taken pre-operatively and at 12 months post-operatively are shown in Figure 4A,B.

With the hope of providing a sustained effect to reduce post-operative fibrosis surrounding the inserted electrode, and to preserve residual hearing at the lower frequencies, a new DEX-eluting electrode (FLEX28 DEX electrode array, MED-EL, Innsbruck, Austria) was used as part of a clinical trial in February 2024
The patient underwent a less-invasive surgical procedure for HP as described previously
The round window membrane was widely exposed by removing the bony over-hang of the round window niche with a low-speed drill.
Subsequently, the electrode was slowly inserted via the round window membrane.

During electrode insertion, intraoperative cochlear microphonics (CM) monitoring was performed to confirm low-frequency functional preservation and to determine the most appropriate electrode position

During surgery, a 500 Hz acoustic stimulus was applied to the external auditory canal, and the CM response was recorded from the first electrode (Ch 1). The maximum response was obtained when the first electrode reached the area responsible for 500 Hz
(C) The first electrode has just reached the area responsible for 500 Hz. The maximum CM reaction has been obtained.
(A) The tip of the electrode has been inserted into the basal turn of the cochlear. As it is still far from the area responsible for the 500 Hz, no CM response is observed.
(B) The first electrode has just reached the area responsible for 1000 Hz. A weak CM reaction is observed.
(D) After full insertion, the first electrode is farther away from the area responsible for 500 Hz, so the response is weaker.

(E) After full insertion, CM responses were taken from the first, third, and fifth electrodes, and the largest response was from the third electrode, which was located in the area responsible for 500 Hz.

claims.text: Residual hearing was well preserved after electrode insertion; hearing preservation was partial (58.6%) and comparable with 22 conventional FLEX28 patients, and an audiogram was taken at 12 months post-operatively. Hearing level with EAS was around 25–35 dB, and speech audiometry improved to 72% for monosyllables and 92% for words. Post-operative impedance was lower and more stable than with conventional electrodes.

evidence.quote: After electrode insertion, residual hearing available for acoustic stimulation was well preserved.
Based on the HP criteria [], HP in this case was regarded as “partial (58.6%).”
HP for this patient was comparable with that for 22 EAS patients using conventional FLEX28 electrodes (Figure 5).
Audiograms taken pre-operatively and at 12 months post-operatively are shown in Figure 4A,B.
Hearing level with EAS is around 25–35 dB (Figure 4C).
Japanese speech audiometry (iCI2004) also improved to 72% (monosyllable perception in quiet) and 92% (word recognition in SN + 10 dB).
The impedance measured by IFT of the patient with the DEX-eluting electrode (FLEX28 DEX) was lower and quite stable compared to that of patients with the conventional FLEX28 electrode (Figure 6).
Post-operative impedance field telemetry (IFT) taken from (A) electrode Ch 1, (B) electrode Ch 5 and (C) electrode Ch 11.
IFT was maintained at a very low level compared with the controls.
